title: New Stanford & Berkeley AI Papers Make Humanoid Robots & Agents Self-Improving!
summary: Two late-October 2026 arXiv breakthroughs target autonomous agent evolution and humanoid robotics stability: GEPA-Curator by Matei Zaharia's team introduces curated learning pipelines for self-improving language agents, while Delay Randomization for Humanoid Trackers widens the command-latency margin for learned humanoid motion controllers.
raw_text: So check this out: while everyone is distracted by big corporate press releases, two super important research papers just hit arXiv that solve massive headaches for AI agents and humanoid robots. First up is GEPA-Curator, co-authored by Databricks co-founder and Berkeley legend Matei Zaharia alongside Zack Yu. Right now, when language agents try to learn from their own past trajectories, they often poison their own training data with sloppy habits. GEPA-Curator builds a strict, automated curation pipeline so language agents can genuinely self-improve over time without degrading. And second, if you love humanoid robots, researchers Shaoqin Li and Yi Sun just published a paper on 'Delay Randomization for Humanoid Trackers'. Here's the problem with bipedal robots: in a computer simulation, motor commands happen instantly, but in the real world, wireless latency and hardware delays make humanoid robots stumble and faceplant. By injecting randomized command delays during training, their controller dramatically widens the latency margin so real-world humanoids can stay balanced even when their onboard compute lags. Small foundational wins like these are what actually make futuristic tech work in the real world!
